rv.q: And that’s precisely what Court Theatre delivers with a blisteringly entertaining new Ron OJ Parson production of August Wilson’s “Two Trains Running” — Wilson’s 1960s play perhaps best known for the defiant, tragicomic line “I want my ham!”
The fine actors here capture the musicality of Wilson’s individual monologues, but there’s a lack of overall shape to rising and falling action.

And Court Theatre’s latest revival of this seminal work — the ninth production of a Wilson play to be directed on its stage by Ron OJ Parson, and brought to vivid life by a cast including many of Chicago’s finest and most enduring actors — is not to be missed.
There are performances here that will last forever “Two Trains Running” is a play one listens to.
Two Trains Running is tantalizingly powerful, filled with brilliant dialogue.
The show is, by turns, funny, touching, infuriating, inspiring and tragic—all fueled by Wilson’s unmatched ability with the easy rhythms of dialog and the idiosyncrasies of quixotic human behavior.
This is an impeccable production of a play whose weaknesses outweigh its considerable strengths.
It is thought-provoking, poignant and yet laugh-out-loud funny.
I have to admit; this is one of my lesser favorites. Although there were funny moments, I found myself cringing through most of the dialogue.

cn.t: Court Theatre delivers a rousing, impeccably performed production of Wilson's Pittsburgh Cycle play, though some critics find the work itself uneven despite its considerable strengths and blisteringly entertaining moments.
